primitives.name: Sprint Start Crouching
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the former the runner crouches down, touching his fingers to the ground, one foot on the mark, the other just behind it.
primitives.latex: $x_{crouch} = x_{mark} + \Delta x$, where $\Delta x$ is the offset of the rear foot
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x_crouch': 'position of crouching stance (m)', 'x_mark': 'starting line position (m)', 'Δx': 'rear foot offset relative to mark (m)'}
primitives.assumptions: Point mass approximation, negligible air resistance, constant acceleration during initial push-off
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when rear foot offset becomes zero ($\Delta x \rightarrow 0$), leading to unstable force distribution

layer2.mapping: GSI - converts biomechanical stance parameters into prior distributions over sprinter's reaction time variability
layer2.telemetry: Reaction time measured from electronic timing systems (seconds)

primitives.name: Pace Knowledge 220
primitives.verbatim_quote: The 220-yard men practise like the 100-yard men, with this exception—that the 220 men must acquire a knowledge of pace which the 100 men do not so certainly need.
primitives.assumptions: Constant average velocity assumption over the entire race distance, ignoring acceleration and deceleration phases
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure mode occurs when pace knowledge is inexact, causing premature exhaustion or loss of lead in final stretch

layer2.mapping: GSE - models state transitions between pacing zones (e.g., early burst vs. controlled endurance)
layer2.telemetry: Instantaneous speed measurements from split times (mph or m/s)

primitives.name: No Turning Until Tape
primitives.verbatim_quote: Don't leave that mark until the pistol goes, and then you go too, and as if Death were after you.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_turn': 'time of turning head (s)', 't_tape': 'time of chest crossing finish line (s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rigid-body rotation model, minimal delay between visual cue and physical response
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violation leads to aerodynamic drag penalties and potential stumbling, degrading final velocity

layer2.mapping: GSI - encodes tactical commitment to final sprint phase, reducing uncertainty about race outcome
layer2.telemetry: Head orientation angle relative to track axis (degrees)

primitives.name: Pace Control 220
primitives.verbatim_quote: But in a 220 the runner should know something of pace as do the longer distance men.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v(t)': 'instantaneous velocity at time t (m/s)', 'Pace_target': 'desired average pace (yd/s)', 'Distance_remaining': 'distance left to cover (m)'}
primitives.assumptions: Continuous adjustment of speed based on remaining distance, assuming linear relationship between effort and velocity
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overestimation of target pace causes early fatigue; underestimation allows trailing competitors to close gap

layer2.mapping: GSE - integrates pace control as a state-transition reward function in dynamic programming models
layer2.telemetry: Running cadence (steps per minute) and stride length variations
